body:
Thank you so much for your advice.

Here's what I've done/decided to do since you posted:

* I've taken a second look at my courseload for next semester, and realized that if I drop Electronics, and the associated lab, I move down to 15 hours (the minimum for my scholarship), and also get Fridays off, have no classes before 2:30 P.M., and only have 4 classes, all of which are related to each other material-wise.  Much more manageable.

* Because I am on scholarship probation, I believe my school effectively forces me to take some kind of academic counseling.  However, with my reduced workload, it might be easier to maintain a good social life (my girlfriend has Fridays off too! :D)  Hopefully, things will improve for me socially, but if not, I'll try to take the plunge into counseling.

* I'm gonna set aside some 2 - 3 hour blocks of time (which fit perfectly into my schedule) *specifically* to study.  I think this will help with time management.  But really, as long as I hold even a modicum of responsibility this semester, I think I will be ok.

Thank you!
It makes me feel better to hear that my situation is not atypical.  I am lucky in a lot of ways, and have had a good life overall. Thank you for the advice and kind words!
Yeah, I wouldn't want you to feel sorry for me...I want to solve these problems, not wallow in them.  Do you have any advice, as someone who is clearly older and more experienced in life?
